extracted.intended_audience: editors, researchers, funders, academic institutions, and other stakeholders assessing journal legitimacy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for assessing whether a scholarly journal or publisher is predatory or pseudo by checking editorial practices, business practices, transparency, indexing/metrics, and red-flag behaviors. Intended to help stakeholders decide whether to submit, cite, or credit publications from a journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of external peer review / publishes most submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Although predatory journals may claim to conduct peer review and mimic the structure of legitimate journals, they publish all or most submitted material without external peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the journal describes transparent peer review processes and whether published papers show evidence of rigorous review; beware of universal acceptance or extremely high acceptance rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to follow standard policies (archiving, COI, errata, transparency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Predatory journals do not follow standard policies advocated by organizations such as WAME, COPE, ICMJE, and CSE regarding archiving of journal content, management of potential conflicts of interest, handling of errata, and transparency of journal processes and policies including fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify explicit policies on digital preservation/archiving, conflict-of-interest declarations, corrections/retractions, and transparent fee/publishing policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggressive mass solicitation and formulaic e-mails
rubrics_metrics.description: A common practice among predatory publishers is sending frequent e-mails to large numbers of individuals soliciting manuscript submission and promising rapid publication for author fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulaic, non-targeted solicitations (not mentioning the recipient's specific research) are a red flag; collect examples of spam solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collects fees but fails to publish promised articles
rubrics_metrics.description: In the most egregious cases, predatory publishers collect publication fees but the promised published articles never appear on the journal web site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors report paying fees without publication, or issues/volumes are missing, treat as strong evidence of predatory behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misleading or counterfeit metrics, fake impact factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher falsely claims one or more of its journals have actual (Thomson-Reuters) impact factors, or advertises impact factors assigned by fake 'impact factor' services, or it uses some made up measure (eg, view factor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify claimed metrics against recognized indexing services (Clarivate/Journal Citation Reports, Scopus, DOAJ) and be suspicious of unfamiliar metric names or private 'impact factors.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Hijacked journals (counterfeit sites impersonating legitimate journals)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Hijacked journals’ refer to the creation of a counterfeit Web site that mimics the Web site of a legitimate journal for the purpose of soliciting submissions and collecting author fees from authors who believe they are sending their work to the legitimate journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare publisher/journal URLs, contact information, and ISSNs with the legitimate journal; check archival records and publisher listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: False claims of indexing or discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher falsely claims to have its content indexed in legitimate abstracting and indexing services or claims that its content is indexed in resources that are not abstracting and indexing services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm indexing claims directly with the named indexing services and search for journal articles in recognized databases and Google Scholar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient or hidden information about author fees (surprise invoices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides insufficient information or hides information about author fees, offering to publish an author's paper and later sending an unanticipated 'surprise' invoice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author fees should be clearly explained on the site, including what the fees cover and when they are charged; lack of fee transparency is a strong warning sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: No or unclear statement about peer review in Instructions for Authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is not mentioned in the Instructions for Authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the Instructions for Authors for explicit description of the type and stages of peer review; absence of such information is suspicious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Little or no information about editor or editorial board
rubrics_metrics.description: Little or no information is provided regarding the editor or editorial board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legitimate journals identify editors and board members with institutional affiliations and expertise; absence or vagueness warrants caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors/staff lack academic information or expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: No academic information is provided regarding the editor, editorial staff, and/or review board members; evidence exists showing that the editor and/or review board members do not possess academic expertise to reasonably qualify them to be publication gatekeepers in the journal's field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify editorial affiliations, publication records, and subject-matter expertise of named editors/board members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner named as editor across all journals (conflict of roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher's owner is identified as the editor of each and every journal published by the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may indicate lack of independent editorial oversight and conflicts of interest; investigate governance and editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: No single individual identified as a journal's editor
rubrics_metrics.description: No single individual is identified as any specific journal's editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A named editor-in-chief or equivalent is an expected feature of legitimate journals; generic or absent editor information is a red flag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate editorial boards across multiple journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more journals have duplicate editorial boards (ie, same editorial board for more than one journal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated board listings across unrelated journals suggest token or fabricated boards designed to lend false legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient number of board members / concocted editorial boards
rubrics_metrics.description: The journals have an insufficient number of board members (eg, 2 or 3 members), have concocted editorial boards (made up names), name scholars on their editorial board without their knowledge or permission or have board members who are prominent researchers but exempt them from any contributions to the journal except the use of their names and/or photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether listed board members acknowledge their roles and whether the board composition is appropriate for the journal's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Little or no geographic diversity on editorial board when claiming international scope
rubrics_metrics.description: There is little or no geographical diversity among the editorial board members, especially for journals that claim to be international in scope or coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A truly international journal typically shows geographic diversity; lack thereof can be an indicator, though this may penalize legitimate journals from LMICs—use cautiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial board engages in gender bias (exclusion of female members)
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial board engages in gender bias (ie, exclusion of any female members).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beall listed this as a potential indicator; WAME cautions that some such criteria can be unreliable and may misidentify legitimate journals, so interpret in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of transparency in publishing operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrates a lack of transparency in publishing operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect clear ownership, governance, editorial processes, policies, and contact information; opacity is a warning sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: No policies or practices for digital preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Has no policies or practices for digital preservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legitimate journals deposit content in long-term archiving programs (eg, CLOCKSS, Portico) and state preservation policies; absence suggests poor commitment to scholarly record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Launches with a large fleet of journals using common templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Begins operations with a large fleet of journals, often using a common template to quickly create each journal's home page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapid creation of many superficially different journals often aims to maximize fee revenue rather than serve scholarly communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blocks search engines or copy-proofs PDFs
rubrics_metrics.description: Does not allow search engines to crawl the published content, preventing the content from being indexed in academic indexes; copy-proofs (locks) their PDFs, thus making it harder to check for plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published content should be discoverable and accessible; technical barriers to indexing or checking content are suspicious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name incongruent with mission or misrepresents origin
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of a journal is incongruent with the journal's mission; the name of a journal does not adequately reflect its origin (eg, a journal with the word 'Canadian' or 'Swiss' in its name when neither the publisher, editor, nor any purported institutional affiliate relates whatsoever to Canada or Switzerland).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether journal title, stated aims, and editorial/publisher location align; misleading names are intended to deceive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sends peer review requests to unqualified reviewers or mis-matches specialty
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher sends spam requests for peer reviews to scholars unqualified to review submitted manuscripts, in the sense that the specialties of the invited reviewers do not match the papers sent to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicitations to review outside one's expertise or generic reviewer requests indicate poor peer review hygiene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient effort to prevent/eliminate author misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher dedicates insufficient resources to preventing and eliminating author misconduct, to the extent that the journal or journals suffer from repeated cases of plagiarism, self-plagiarism, image manipulation, and the like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence of plagiarism checks, retraction/correction policies, and editorial action when misconduct occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uses author-suggested reviewers without vetting
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher asks the corresponding author for suggested reviewers and the publisher subsequently uses the suggested reviewers without sufficiently vetting their qualifications or authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check peer review practices—use of unvetted suggested reviewers is associated with reviewer fraud and compromised review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-publishes papers already published elsewhere without credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-publish papers already published in other venues/outlets without providing appropriate credits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duplicate publication without attribution indicates weak editorial oversight and unethical practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boastful language and false claims of prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: Use boastful language claiming to be a 'leading publisher' even though the publisher may only be a startup or a novice organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grandiose claims without independent corroboration (indexing, society sponsorship) are suspicious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misrepresentation of operational location (mail-drops, PO boxes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate in a Western country chiefly for the purpose of functioning as a vanity press for scholars in a developing country (eg, utilizing a mail drop address or PO box address in the United States, while actually operating from a developing country).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify physical address and contact details; use WHOIS and other records if necessary to confirm operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal or no copyediting or proofreading
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide minimal or no copyediting or proofreading of submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poorly edited articles with frequent typographical or formatting errors suggest lax editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishes non-academic content (lay essays, polemics, pseudo-science)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish papers that are not academic at all, eg, essays by lay people, polemical editorials, or obvious pseudo-science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess article content quality relative to scholarly norms for the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact page lacks verifiable contact details or hides location
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a 'contact us' page that only includes a web form or an e-mail address, and the publisher hides or does not reveal its location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legitimate publishers provide institutional contact information, postal addresses, and telephone numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies author guidelines verbatim from other publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher copies 'authors guidelines' verbatim (or with minor editing) from other publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for generic or obviously copied policies; tailor-made guidelines and policies are markers of legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient contact information or misrepresented headquarters
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher lists insufficient contact information, including contact information that does not clearly state the headquarters location or misrepresents the headquarters location (eg, through the use of addresses that are actually mail drops).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corroborate contact info with institutional pages or third-party listings; misrepresentation is a red flag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessively broad journal scope to attract submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher publishes journals that are excessively broad (eg, Journal of Education) in order to attract more articles and gain more revenue from author fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very broad or generic scopes with the aim of maximizing submissions can indicate commercial motives over scholarly focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combines disparate fields unnaturally
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher publishes journals that combine two or more fields not normally treated together (eg, International Journal of Business, Humanities and Technology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unusual combinations of fields without clear interdisciplinary rationale may signal scope-driven revenue strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requires copyright transfer despite charging authors
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher charges authors for publishing but requires transfer of copyright and retains copyright on journal content. Or the publisher requires the copyright transfer upon submission of manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open access and author-pays models ordinarily allow authors to retain copyright or use open licenses; demanding transfer while charging fees is problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poorly maintained website (dead links, misspellings, grammatical errors)
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher has poorly maintained Web sites, including dead links, prominent misspellings and grammatical errors on the Web site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess site quality; persistent errors and broken links indicate lack of professional standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized use of licensed images
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher makes unauthorized use of licensed images on their Web site, taken from the open web, without permission or licensing from the copyright owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copyright violations on the site signal unethical practices and lack of legal/ethical oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOAJ seal requirement: permanent identifiers (eg, DOIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive the DOAJ seal, journals must provide permanent identifiers (eg, DOIs) in the papers published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of DOIs is expected for stable scholarly records; absence may indicate weak infrastructure or predatory practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOAJ seal requirement: provide article metadata to DOAJ
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive the DOAJ seal, journals must provide DOAJ with article metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplying metadata supports discoverability and indexing; refusal or omission undermines transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOAJ seal requirement: deposit content with long-term preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive the DOAJ seal, journals must deposit content with a long-term digital preservation or archiving program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archiving ensures long-term availability; lack of archiving is concerning.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOAJ seal requirement: embed machine-readable CC licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive the DOAJ seal, journals must embed machine-readable CC licensing information in articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Machine-readable licensing supports reuse and clarity of rights; absence reduces openness.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOAJ seal requirement: allow generous reuse per CC BY/SA/NC
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive the DOAJ seal, journals must allow generous reuse and mixing of content, in accordance with a CC BY, CC BY-SA or CC BY-NC license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the journal's copyright/licensing policy for compliance with open access norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOAJ seal requirement: have a registered deposit policy
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive the DOAJ seal, journals must have a deposit policy registered with a deposit policy registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registered deposit policy indicates commitment to preservation and author rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think. Check. Submit: recognition and discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you or your colleagues know the journal? Have you read any articles in the journal before? Is it easy to discover the latest papers in the journal?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarity and discoverability are positive indicators; lack of prior exposure does not prove predatory status but warrants further checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think. Check. Submit: clear publisher identity and contactability
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the publisher name clearly displayed on the journal Web site? Can you contact the publisher by telephone, e-mail, and post?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparent and verifiable publisher identity and reachable contact channels are expected of legitimate journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think. Check. Submit: clarity about peer review type
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the journal clear about the type of peer review it uses?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legitimate journals describe whether peer review is single-blind, double-blind, open, etc., and outline editorial handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think. Check. Submit: indexing in services you use
rubrics_metrics.description: Are articles indexed in services that you use?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing in relevant, recognized databases increases discoverability and legitimacy; verify indexing claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think. Check. Submit: clarity about fees and explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it clear what fees will be charged? Does the journal site explain what these fees are for and when they will be charged?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparent fee schedules and explanations of services covered help distinguish legitimate APC models from predatory fee practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think. Check. Submit: recognizable editorial board and member endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you recognize the editorial board? Have you heard of the editorial board members? Do the editorial board members mention the journal on their own Web sites?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check board member profiles and whether they acknowledge the journal on institutional pages; unacknowledged listings may be fabricated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think. Check. Submit: publisher membership in recognized industry initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the publisher a member of a recognized industry initiative (eg, COPE)? If the journal is open access, is it listed in the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ)? If the journal is open access, does the publisher belong to OASPA?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership in COPE, DOAJ listing, or OASPA affiliation are positive signals, though not absolute guarantees of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning sign: no information on author fees in Instructions for Authors
rubrics_metrics.description: No information as to whether there are author fees in the Instructions for Authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be able to find APC or other fee information readily; absence is problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning sign: journal web site not easily accessible in search engines
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal Web site is not easily accessible in an Internet search (could be a problem in a legitimate journal in a low- or middle-income locale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poor discoverability is a concern; consider context (new or LMIC journals) and corroborate with other checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning sign: unusual publication volume (too few, too many, or variable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal publishes either an unusually small, unusually large, or markedly variable numbers of articles each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inconsistent or implausible publishing volumes can indicate opportunistic publishing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning sign: promised turnaround times unrealistically rapid
rubrics_metrics.description: Promised routine turnaround times for review and publication are so rapid that they seem 'too good to be true' and would be unlikely to encompass the time necessary for true peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very short review-to-publication timelines (days to weeks) for standard peer review raise concerns about review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning sign: no response to editorial contact within a few days
rubrics_metrics.description: You do not receive a response to e-mail or telephone messages sent to the editor or journal office within a few days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of timely or any response suggests poor operations or nonexistent editorial staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning sign: journal name imitates an established journal
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the journal is very similar to the name of a well-known, established journal with a good reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name imitation (near-duplicates of established journals) is often used to mislead authors and readers—verify ISSN and publisher identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning sign: atypical publication fees (much higher or much lower)
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication fees are atypical for the scholarly publishing industry (much higher or much lower fees can both signal problems [with recognition that journals in low- or middle-income countries may have legitimately low fees]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare fees to disciplinary norms and investigate what services fees cover; both extremes may indicate issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning sign: difficulty finding articles in databases/search
rubrics_metrics.description: It is difficult to identify articles published in the journal when searching Google Scholar or other databases (with recognition that new journals or those in low- or middle-income countries may face lags in indexing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search multiple databases and consider journal age; persistent invisibility is concerning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning sign: missing author affiliations or contact info in published articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about author affiliations and/or contact information is not present in published articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author affiliation and contact details are standard scholarly practice; their absence reduces accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning sign: listed editorial board member unaware of affiliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Someone you know listed on the editorial board or journal staff, when you query them about the journal, is unaware of their supposed affiliation with the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directly contact listed board members to confirm affiliations; fabricated listings are strong evidence of misconduct.
